anchors.description: Oval white lavatory basin set in the granite vanity counter; measured across its long axis between the visible left and right rim edges.
anchors.visible_evidence: The white oval basin and its rim are fully visible on the counter; both extreme left and right rim edges lie on the visible oval boundary at similar depth.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Model unknown; standard oval bath basins are 17-19 in (0.43-0.48 m) wide, and the visible boundary may be the granite cutout if the sink is undermounted.

anchors.description: Vertical distance from the tile floor at the makeup-chair knee space to the top face of the granite vanity countertop.
anchors.visible_evidence: Granite countertop top face at the right end of the vanity is visible; tile floor is visible below the chair skirt in approximately the same image column, giving a near-vertical pair spanning the vanity height.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Custom cabinetry without labels; US bathroom vanity tops are commonly 32-36 in (0.81-0.91 m) above the finished floor, and makeup vanities are sometimes lower.
